characters.summary: Rayman is a limbless platforming hero who fights using his telescopic fists, a helicopter hair-glide, and various magical or mechanical power-ups granted by fairies. He can attack at range, swing from purple rings, and traverse dangerous obstacles using acrobatics and vehicles.

sources.supports: Basic character mechanics, origins, and gameplay attributes.
Telescopic fist and Betilla the fairy's powers.

Limbless body with head, hands and feet 'invisibly linked to his torso'; throwing his fists as projectiles; spinning his hair like a helicopter rotor to slow his descent; Rabbids taking his fists in the handheld Raving Rabbids.

Telescopic fist granted by Betilla in Rayman (1995); gold fists double its power, speed fists throw faster, charging increases power; grappling fist; replaced by energy-ball shooting in Rayman 2; returns in Rayman 3 and Origins/Legends.
Final battle of Rayman (1995): Mr Dark steals Rayman's fist power, Electoons return it, and Rayman defeats Mr Dark's three hybrid-monster forms, the last with a final punch to the head.

The super helicopter is a temporary power-up (Musician's flask in Rayman, Ly in Rayman 2) that 'allows you to fly while retaining control of your direction', as opposed to the normal helicopter glide.

sources.supports: Metroid Dread storyline, climax, and Metroid Suit awakening.
Details on the Hyper Beam and energy draining abilities.

After fully awakening her Metroid DNA while fighting Raven Beak, Samus's Gravity Suit turns into the Metroid Suit; the Hyper Beam penetrates terrain, is the only weapon that kills X Parasites outright, and was used twice to destroy Raven Beak X; absorbing the X with Quiet Robe's DNA neutralized the suit.

Awakened 'full Metroid ability' drains a large amount of energy from Raven Beak and his spaceship; the energy-draining suit would stop her jet from leaving intact; Quiet Robe's sacrifice returns her suit to normal.

unknowns: Whether she can voluntarily trigger the Metroid Suit without absorbing X Parasite DNA.
Whether she stole Raven Beak's beam is fan speculation; the in-game Samus Screen says the Hyper Beam combines her own Arm Cannon abilities.

characters.summary: Phazon Suit Samus is the corrupted form gained after defeating the Omega Pirate in Metroid Prime. The suit shields her from Blue Phazon toxicity and enables the devastating Phazon Beam used to destroy Metroid Prime.

mechanisms: Enhanced damage resistance against radioactive/corrosive hazards

weaknesses: Corrosive Phazon energy corrupts biological hosts over time
Vulnerable to energy overloads
characters.formDifferences: Corrupts the Varia Suit with radioactive Phazon energy, granting immunity to Blue Phazon pools and empowering the arm cannon with the Phazon Beam.

sources.supports: Metroid Prime storyline, Omega Pirate battle, and Phazon Suit acquisition.
Phazon beam mechanics and hazard immunities.

Formed when the Omega Pirate fell on Samus and Phazon seeped into her suit; complete protection from Blue Phazon but more potent Phazon still damages; dramatically increased shielding; enables Hyper-Mode and the Phazon Beam required to defeat Metroid Prime; Metroid Prime pulls the suit off after its defeat and later becomes Dark Samus.

unknowns: Long-term systemic effects of Phazon integration prior to its extraction by Metroid Prime.
Gemini's feat 'absorbs concentrated Phazon energy to overload enemy targets' is not described in the opened source and was not kept.
